name: William W. Sewall
role: Co-manager of Theodore Roosevelt's Elkhorn ranch
bio: William W. Sewall was put in charge of Theodore Roosevelt's new ranch about thirty miles down the river, the Elkhorn, with Wilmot Dow in August 1884, and an August 1885 account describes the two men and their wives welcoming visitors there. In late March 1886 he and Dow went with Roosevelt in pursuit of the men who had stolen Roosevelt's boat, overtaking them about a hundred miles down the river. In August 1886 he served on a stockgrowers' committee arranging round-up and line-riding, and in October 1886 he and Dow were to leave with their families for Maine.
